releases.body:
### Non-blocking changeset hardening

* Legacy HITL token migration is now **strict**: a pre-v0.12 token is refreshed
  only when its legacy `action_type`+`targets` signature verifies. A tampered
  signature fails both payloads and is refused.
* `targets` and `action_type` are derived from `operations` when a proposal is
  read, so the UI/summary cannot disagree with the guard/package changeset even
  if the legacy columns are edited directly.
* Pending/approved legacy `other` rows are marked `failed` during migration with
  an explicit “re-propose with create/edit/delete operations” reason.
* Local-run completion now compares **content hashes** per target: an identical
  write is a real no-op (`NO TARGET CHANGES`), and a content change with a
  restored mtime is still detected.
* `derive_package()` refuses more than 100 operations defensively.
* Added a source-level UI test for the per-operation proposal chips.

### Existing approved proposals survive the changeset migration

* A HITL approval token issued before v0.12 was bound to `action_type` +
  `targets`. The changeset payload now binds `operations`, so an old token would
  have failed on claim/run and stranded a human approval. `claim_execution()` and
  `_prepare_execution()` now refresh the token from the **stored approval**
  (status, approver, seven-day window) when the signature no longer matches, and
  bind the fresh token to the current changeset. A legacy-token test covers the
  claim path.

### Guard fails closed for an executing proposal with no operations

* A legacy/invalid `executing` row whose `operations` list is empty now makes
  the guard target scope ambiguous instead of returning an empty scope. Writes
  are refused rather than silently allowed anywhere in the project allowlist.
  This can only happen for a pre-v0.12 `other` row or a corrupt row; typed
  changesets always carry operations.

### Breaking: proposals are typed changesets

* A proposal now carries **`operations`**, one `{path, op}` entry per target
  (`create`/`edit`/`delete`). One proposal can mix all three and is applied as a
  single atomic changeset, so a change that adds a file and edits another no
  longer needs a proposal chain. `action_type` is only a derived summary
  (`mixed` when the operations differ).
* `create()`/the REST envelope/the `perun-proposals_propose` MCP tool now require
  `operations`; the old `action_type` + `targets` input is removed. Existing DB
  rows are migrated once from their typed fields; `other` rows become invalid.
* `_assert_action_targets()`, `derive_package()`, the guard, the local prompt and
  the post-run check all use each target’s own operation. `guard_delete_file`
  requires a `delete` operation on that exact target; write/edit are refused for
  a delete target. A package containing a delete remains operator-only.
* The Shared-tab proposal row renders per-operation chips (`create path`,
  `edit path`, `delete path`) and shows `mixed` when the changeset differs.
* Tests cover mixed create+edit, mixed create+delete, mixed local execution,
  duplicate/invalid operations, legacy-row migration, and the existing package
  approval/rollback paths.

### One operator inbox

* Settings no longer mounts a second full copy of the "Needs you" inbox. The
  dedicated `#/attention` page is the canonical inbox; Settings now has a short
  card that links to it. This removes the duplicated panel/count and the extra
  30-second poller that ran while the Settings view was open.

### Missing package manifest fails closed

* A package with an empty/missing derived manifest can no longer be peer-approved,
  and the operator apply path fails closed instead of skipping the manifest
  comparison. A valid pending package always carries its server-derived
  operations; an empty manifest means the row/archive pair is not trustworthy.

### Typed delete enforcement in the guard

* `guard_delete_file` now requires a **delete proposal in `executing` state**;
  a chat session or an edit/create run cannot call it. During a delete run,
  `guard_write_file`/`guard_edit_file` are refused, so a delete cannot be
  replaced by a write. The `perunchat` agent permissions already deny delete
  outright; this is the guard-level backstop for every tool path.

### Delete packages need the local operator

* A package whose derived manifest contains a `delete` operation can no longer
  be approved by a peer/room-owner MCP call. Only the local dashboard operator
  (`operator=True`) or the explicit `policy_auto_approve` path may apply it.
  This closes the gap where the chat persona (room owner) could approve a
  remotely staged delete without the human seeing it.

### Hardening

* The modern MCP `server/discover` grace window is now 5 s (was 3 s), so a cold
  Python MCP server is not incorrectly forced onto the legacy handshake.
* Stored package archives are `flush()`ed and `fsync()`ed before the atomic
  rename, so a crash cannot leave a zero-length or partial approved artifact.

### Security: chat persona cannot delete files

* The `perunchat` agent permissions now deny `<server>_guard_delete_file`
  (alongside write/edit), and the prompt names delete as forbidden. The guarded
  delete tool was added for the local `perun-shared` executor; without this
  deny, the room persona's broad guard allow would have let it delete a project
  file through the chat tool surface. `perun-shared` keeps delete so an approved
  `delete` proposal can execute.

### Legacy package helpers removed

* Removed `package_handoff.validate_package()` / `apply_package()`. The external
  handoff has a single production path now: `derive_package()` computes the typed
  pre/post manifest and `apply_operations()` applies it atomically with rollback.
  Their tests were converted to the typed functions, including a mid-write
  rollback case and an external-dependency rejection.

### Follow-up audit cleanup

* The shared-project prompt note no longer says "you may not execute tools";
  it now explicitly permits the read-only `perun-guard_guard_*` inspection tools
  and the `perun-proposals_*` coordination tools, while still forbidding direct
  edits, shell, web and subagents.
* The per-proposal package lock map is a `WeakValueDictionary`, so it cannot
  grow without bound over the life of a long-running bridge.
* The proposal row uses a block `<div class="intent">` instead of a `<span>`
  wrapping the package `<details>` preview, making the generated HTML valid.
* `validate_package()`/`apply_package()` are marked as deprecated compatibility
  helpers; the production handoff uses `derive_package()`/`apply_operations()`.
